title: priya-shah-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-04.json
content:
On-call scratchpad - 2026-03-04 (Priya Shah)

Summary:
- Night shift quiet overall; two pages early morning related to degraded API p99 latency.
- Major follow-ups logged for INC-2431 (partial throttling on internal gateway) - see notes below.
- Small config drift discovered in autoscaler rule for kafka-consumer-prod (needs fix).

Rotation / contacts:
- Primary: Priya Shah (me)
- Secondary: Ethan Park
- Pager duty schedule: 03:00-11:00 PT (me), 11:00-19:00 PT (Ethan)
- Slack oncall channel: #sre-oncall

Timeline / pages:
- 02:18 - Page: "API p99 spike" - alerted by synthetic job (api-health-check) reporting p99 > 1200ms for /v1/generate on us-west1.
  - Initial triage: checked grafana (latency by route + pod). Noted increased queue length on model-proxy service and elevated CPU on rp-model-03.
  - Action: Scaled model-proxy deployment + drained one rp-model-03 pod for restart.
  - 02:34: latency partially recovered to ~420ms p99.
  - 02:47: Another spike, coincident with a burst of small requests from client-service X (sustained short-lived traffic pattern).
  - Mitigation: Applied ephemeral rate-limit on client-service X via routing rule (10rps) - immediate improvement.
  - Postmortem TODO: determine cause of burst from client-service X, add higher-fidelity throttling rules for noisy clients.

- 04:05 - Page: "Gateway 502s" - internal gateway returning 502 for some downstream calls.
  - Investigation: Gateway logs showed upstream timeouts to authz service (authz-prod) around 03:58-04:03, coincident with a rolling deploy.
  - Rollback: Rollout finished by infra-team at 04:12, 502s cleared.
  - Follow-up: ask infra to ensure canary window extended to 5m for authz service and add alert for deploy-induced error-rate.

Incident (INC-2431) - partial throttling on internal gateway
- What happened: Around 02:10-03:00, internal gateway started returning 429/502 intermittently to some model inference routes. Root cause likely a combination of: a) sudden short burst from client-service X, b) an autoscaler mis-scaling for model-proxy under short-burst pattern, c) a routing rule that didn't correctly rate-limit noisy client.
- Impact: ~6% of requests for /v1/generate on us-west1 experienced elevated latency or errors during the window; no data loss.
- Immediate mitigations: scaled model-proxy, restart of rp-model-03, applied ephemeral routing rate-limit.
- Short-term follow-ups (owners + rough ETA):
  - Priya: write up initial incident timeline + attach graphs (by 2026-03-05).
  - Ethan: verify autoscaler config for model-proxy (min/max/metrics) and propose changes to better handle short bursts (by 2026-03-06).
  - Mia: investigate client-service X traffic pattern and coordinate with their team to add client-side backoff (by 2026-03-07).
  - Infra: ensure deploy canary window for authz service increased and add deploy->error surge alert (requested via SRE-512).
- Long-term actions: add prefix/KV cache metrics surfaced to infra dashboards; implement per-client token-bucket throttling in routing layer.

Runbook TODOs / tech debt spotted during triage:
- Update model-proxy autoscaler runbook: include guidance for handling short, high-burst traffic patterns (priority: high).
- Add a synthetic that simulates client bursts to validate autoscaler behavior (priority: medium).
- Add a paging rule for deploy-induced authz errors that notifies infra and oncall simultaneously (priority: medium).
- Document steps to apply ephemeral routing rule and roll back (small, add to runbook).

Commands / quick snippets I ran (notes for post-incident reconstruction):
- kubectl -n prod get hpa model-proxy -o yaml  # check autoscaler metrics
- kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/rp-model-03
- curl -H 'x-client-id: client-service-x' https://gateway.prod.internal/v1/health -v  # reproduce headers used by client

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- The autoscaler appears to use average CPU over 2m window - that's smoothing out short bursts. Need a second metric (queue length or request concurrency) or a faster window.
- Ephemeral routing limits helped immediately; should consider templated limit profiles per client tier.
- Consider a short-term patch: allow autoscaler to scale more aggressively for model-proxy when queue length metric > threshold.

Communication / docs to send:
- Draft a quick incident summary to post to #sre-incident with timeline and owner list (Priya will draft).
- Follow up with client-service X team (cc: Mia) to request logs and throttling plan.

Next-day priorities (for my follow-up shift / handoff):
- Finalize incident writeup + attach graphs (due 2026-03-05 EOD).
- Merge autoscaler changes or create RFC for metric change (ETA: 2026-03-10).
- Add runbook snippets for ephemeral routing rule (short doc).

Misc small items / reminders:
- Check quota for ephemeral rate-limit rules (Slack infra ticket open?).
- Confirm with telemetry team that we have fine-grained per-client metrics (request rate by client-id).
- Mark INC-2431 as high priority in tracker and link postmortem when done.

End of scratchpad.
